text:
alex: Heads up — ran into a weird `redwoodctl` auth + local testing coupling in WSL2 this morning. Installed redwoodctl via apt inside WSL, but when I ran `redwoodctl login` it opened Edge on Windows, completed auth, then the CLI printed 'no credentials found' and didn't persist anything.

nina: Oof, cross-OS home dir confusion. Where is the binary and what's $HOME inside the shell you used?

alex: Binary is /usr/bin/redwoodctl (apt package). $HOME is /home/alex. I can see a cached file at /mnt/c/Users/Alex/.redwood/creds.json created by the Windows browser flow, but nothing in ~/.config/redwood.

theo: That's the crux — the browser flow uses the Windows callback and the Windows installer writes creds to the Windows config dir, while the linux binary reads ~/.config/redwood. Different stores.

alex: Error output:```
$ redwoodctl login
Opening system browser...
Authentication complete.
Error: credential not found in config dir /home/alex/.config/redwood
```

nina: Two practical fixes: 1) set REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR to point at /mnt/c/Users/Alex/.redwood before running the CLI so both sides see the same files, or 2) install the linux package inside the same OS as the browser (so both write/read same location).

alex: I tried option 1 but `redwoodctl profiles list` still showed none until I copied profiles.json from ~/.config/redwood to the windows path. Looks like profiles aren't auto-migrated.

theo: Profiles + local runtime state (sockets, cache) all live in the config dir. No automatic syncing across OSes. We'll need to doc the migration steps.

alex: Also ran into a follow-up: `redwoodctl local serve --socket /mnt/c/tmp/rw.sock` failed with EACCESS and the server later couldn't bind. Switching to unix socket under /tmp fixed it.

nina: Right — when running under WSL, prefer unix sockets on the WSL filesystem. Windows paths have different permission/locking semantics and can break file descriptors.

alex: Workaround summary I used: 1) install linux binary in WSL via official tarball, 2) export REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=/home/alex/.config/redwood, 3) run `redwoodctl login --device` if the browser callback doesn't route to WSL networking, 4) use /tmp/redwood.sock for local serve. That combination finally gave me a clean local dev loop.

theo: Suggest we add a small onboarding blurb: recommended WSL install path, `--device` fallback for flaky callback, note about explicit REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR when mixing windows/linux installs, and a tip to avoid mounting sockets on /mnt/c.

docs-bot: Referenced docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/redwoodctl#authentication (no WSL section yet) :page_facing_up:

alex: Can someone add a short WSL checklist to the devex onboarding page? Would have saved me 30 minutes. :)

ops-bot: Created DOCS-1139: "redwoodctl WSL troubleshooting and auth/device-flow FAQ" (assigned: nina).

nina: I'll draft the page and include a tiny migration script to copy profiles/credentials between paths and an example `systemd`-like wrapper for running local serve on WSL.

alex: Thanks! Also filing a tiny CLI UX note: if the binary detects it's running under WSL and finds creds in a windows path, prompt the user about copying them automatically. Low friction fix.

theo: Good idea. I'll add a feature request to the redwoodctl repo.
